study.title: Acupuncture With deqi Modulates the Hemodynamic Response and Functional Connectivity of the Prefrontal-Motor Cortical Network
study.study_design: Quasi-experimental within-subject design with five conditions (pre-acupuncture rest control, pre-manipulation tactile control, acupuncture manipulation, post-manipulation tactile control, post-acupuncture rest control)
study.randomization: Random acupuncture on the right or left hand at the Hegu acupoint was conducted to avoid bias of acupuncture site; no mention of formal randomization of conditions
study.population: Twenty healthy right-handed volunteers (23.9 ± 1.5 years old, age range from 22 to 28 years, twelve males and eight females)
study.inclusion_criteria: Right-handed, normal intelligence, no history of mental illness, no brain damage caused by long-term medication, naive to acupuncture (never experienced an acupuncture treatment)
study.exclusion_criteria: History of mental illness, brain damage caused by long-term medication, prior acupuncture experience

arms.dropouts: 3 subjects excluded due to poor fNIRS signal quality (>50% channels rejected): S14, S18, S20

conditions.scan_context: Subject awake and resting, no needle inserted
Sterile acupuncture needle inserted at Hegu acupoint to a certain depth without twisting; subject awake and resting for 5 min before acupuncture twisting
Active twirling manipulation at Hegu acupoint for 2 min at 2 Hz
Needle kept at Hegu acupoint without twist; subject awake in resting state for 5 min
Needle removed; subject awake and resting for 5 min without movement

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: NirScan, Danyang Huichuang Medical Equipment Co., Ltd.
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Continuous wave fNIRS; near-infrared light of three different wavelengths (740, 808, and 850 nm)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: approximately 22 min total (5 + 5 + 2 + 5 + 5 min across five conditions)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: MATLAB 17.0 (MathWorks, United States); GRETNA (GRaph thEoreTical Network Analysis toolbox); AtlasViewer; BrainNet Viewer; tMCimg (Monte-Carlo photon transmitted software)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: PCA-based motion artifact correction; noisy outlier epochs rejected if absolute Z-score of HbO concentration was larger than 3; subjects excluded if >50% of channels rejected
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: 0.01–0.2 Hz Butterworth bandpass filter; 0.1 Hz notch filter (Mayer wave removal)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: Functional connectivity (Pearson's correlation coefficients of HbO time series)
statistical_thresholds_exact: Two-sample t-tests, FDR correction, alpha = 0.05 and statistical power >0.95 (acupuncture responsive area mapping)
Paired t-tests, FDR corrected, alpha = 0.05 and statistical power >0.95 (region-to-region functional connectivity comparisons)
Paired t-tests, **p < 0.01 and statistical power >0.95, *p < 0.05 and statistical power >0.8 (graph theory metrics)
One-way ANOVA, post-hoc t-tests with FDR correction
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: False discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons
neuroimaging_methods.additional_notes: 48 measurement channels; 15 light sources and 16 detectors; source-detector distance 3 cm; sampling rate 9 Hz; spatial registration to MNI space using Tsuzuki et al. (2007) approach; HbO and HbR obtained via modified Beer-Lambert law; HMS algorithm applied to separate functional brain activity from systemic components; sliding window technique with 5 s window length without overlap for epoch calculation

extraction_notes.note: Exact numeric mean ± SEM values for the deqi index bar chart (Figure 3) are not reported in the text. Values are only visible from the figure bar heights, which cannot be precisely read from PDF.
Individual deqi subscale scores (suan, ma, zhang, tong, zouchuan, zhong) per condition are not reported in the main text; referenced as Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided.
The specific channel number(s) used as the 'typical PFC channel' in Figures 4A-D are not identified in the main text.

Exact channel labels and MNI coordinates of the 8 acupuncture responsive channels are referenced as 'Supplementary Figure 2A' which was not provided. However, the paper states they were distributed over bilateral PFC and bilateral motor cortex.

Exact numeric values for the functional connectivity matrix (Figure 6) are partially readable from the figure labels (e.g., 0.42, 0.52, 0.24, 0.28, 0.32, 0.36, 0.40, 0.51, 0.52, 0.40) but full precision cannot be guaranteed from PDF figure extraction.
Exact numeric values for the shortest path length and global efficiency (Figure 7) are not reported in the text; they are only visible from figure bar charts across sparsity thresholds.

Supplementary Figure 1 (fNIRS preprocessing pipeline), Supplementary Figure 2 (acupuncture responsive channel labels and HbO power change map), Supplementary Figure 3 (correlation scatter plots for PFC and motor cortex vs. deqi index), Supplementary Figures 4 and 5 (channel-to-channel FC matrices and region-pair comparisons), Supplementary Figure 6 (local efficiency, clustering coefficient, small-world metrics), and Supplementary Table 1 (individual deqi index data) are all referenced but not provided.

The study design is within-subject quasi-experimental. There is only one arm (all subjects undergo all conditions). The 'controls' are within-session time-matched conditions, not separate randomized control arms. The arm structure reflects this within-subject design.

The paper states 'random acupuncture on the right or left hand at the Hegu acupoint was conducted to avoid the bias of acupuncture site' but does not report whether this was formally randomized or counterbalanced, nor does it report the split of right vs. left.

The paper does not report whether the correlation between PFC HbO power change and deqi index (r=0.234, p<0.05, statistical power >0.50) was corrected for multiple comparisons across channels or whether it represents a single averaged PFC measure.
Adverse events and safety monitoring are not discussed in the paper. No statement confirming absence of adverse events was found.
Expectancy and credibility measures were not assessed. The study only assessed deqi sensation post-manipulation. This is noted as a limitation in terms of subjective/psychological confounds.

The paper describes the tactile controls (needle inserted without twisting) as 'controls' but these involve real needle penetration at the same acupoint. They are not sham acupuncture in the traditional sense (no deceptive device, no non-acupoint). This should be interpreted carefully in meta-analysis classification.

Figure 6 connectivity values (e.g., 0.28, 0.24, 0.32, 0.36, 0.40, 0.42, 0.51, 0.52) are read from figure labels and may not represent all connection types precisely. The exact number of significant edges (red lines in Figure 6B) cannot be counted precisely from the PDF figure.

The coordinate values extracted for each channel ROI are from Table 2 (channel MNI coordinates), not from a traditional neuroimaging peak coordinate table. These represent fNIRS channel locations, not fMRI activation peaks. They should not be used in standard coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis (e.g., ALE) without acknowledging this methodological difference.
The paper does not report trial registration.

The paper reports 'acupuncture responsive channels, n = 8' but does not list these 8 channels by number in the main text, referring to Supplementary Figure 2A for channel labels. The ROI assignment can be inferred from Table 2 for channels in PFC and Motor ROIs.
